subtopics.title: Rejuvenation — A River Made Young Again

questions.question: Base level is best defined as:
options: The height of the river's source
The lowest level to which a river can erode, ultimately sea level
The deepest pool in the river
The average depth of the channel

questions.question: Rejuvenation means a river:
options: Dries up in its old age
Starts meandering for the first time
Regains erosive energy and cuts downward vigorously again, because its relationship with base level has changed

questions.question: The two main families of causes of rejuvenation are:
options: A drop in base level, such as a eustatic fall in sea level, and uplift of the land

questions.question: After rejuvenation begins, the knickpoint:
options: Stays fixed at the river mouth
Retreats upstream, like a zip opening from the mouth toward the source

questions.question: South Africa's textbook example of a knickpoint waterfall is:
Paired river terraces form when:
options: Two rivers flow side by side
Glaciers carve benches into the valley
The rejuvenated river slices through its own floodplain, stranding the old valley floor as matching benches on both sides

questions.question: The valley-in-a-valley form seen in cross-section is:
options: A young, steep-sided valley incised into the floor of an old, broad valley
Two parallel valleys separated by a ridge
A valley blocked by a landslide
A dry valley beside a wet one

questions.question: Entrenched meanders differ from ingrown meanders in that entrenched meanders are:
options: Symmetric, cut straight down by fast vertical erosion, while ingrown meanders are asymmetric from slower incision with sideways shifting

subtopics.title: River Capture — The Theft of a River

questions.question: The weapon by which the stronger river achieves capture is:
options: Headward erosion — extending its source backward through the watershed toward its neighbour's channel

questions.question: A river gains the erosive advantage that leads to capture if it has:
options: A steeper gradient, softer rock or higher rainfall — and therefore more erosive energy
A longer course to the sea

questions.question: The misfit stream is:
options: The stream that did the capturing
The dry valley through the ridge
The beheaded lower course of the victim — a stream far too small for the broad valley it occupies

questions.question: After capture, the captor stream often rejuvenates because:
options: Its discharge suddenly increases, boosting its energy for renewed downcutting

subtopics.title: Significance for People and Reading the Map

questions.question: Road and rail builders favour wind gaps because they offer:
options: A ready-made pass through high ground, without climbing the ridge

questions.question: Old towns and farms often line river terraces because terraces are:
options: Flat, fertile and above flood level
The only source of drinking water

questions.question: On a topographic map, strong evidence of river capture is:
options: A wide floodplain with oxbow lakes
A sharp elbow bend plus a dry notch in the ridge and a thin stream in an oversized valley downstream
A delta at the river mouth
Closely spaced contours along the watershed

questions.question: A deep, narrow incised gorge attracts dam builders because:
options: A narrow gorge means a short, cheap dam wall holding back a large volume

subtopics.title: The Old River Wins the Lottery

questions.question: In the pensioner picture, winning the lottery stands for:
options: The old river suddenly regaining a young river's cutting energy — rejuvenation

questions.question: The river's finish line — the floor of its world — is:
The two ways the gap between river and finish line can widen are:
options: The sea falls — as in an ice age — or the land rises through uplift

subtopics.title: Four Clues the River Got Young

questions.question: The clue that crawls upstream year by year is:
options: The knickpoint with its waterfall, chewing its way toward the source

questions.question: Terraces come in matching pairs like bunk beds because:
options: Each rejuvenation strands the same old floodplain surface on both sides of the new trench
Floods deposit evenly on both banks

questions.question: In the terrace staircase, the OLDEST terrace is found:
The sunken snake — a winding gorge like the Blyde River canyon — forms when:
options: An earthquake splits the rock in curves
The sea floods a winding valley
A young river learns to meander in rock
A meandering river keeps its loops while cutting straight down with renewed energy

subtopics.title: The Neighbour Who Stole the Pipe

questions.question: In the crime-scene walk, the signed confession on the map is:
options: The elbow of capture — the unnatural right-angle bend where the stolen water turns into the thief's valley

questions.question: The misfit stream is like one learner in a hall built for eight hundred because:
options: The valley was carved by the much fuller river it used to be
The hall was built too big

questions.question: The wind gap is:
options: The abandoned dry stretch of valley through the high ground where the river used to flow

questions.question: For people, the aftermath of capture typically means:
options: The victim's valley gets more floods
Farms on the captor side gain water assurance while towns on the victim's lower course watch their river and boreholes shrink
